name: Utah

supervised_quote: Practice Driving Hours Required : 40 (10 after sunset)
holding_quote: Have held your learner permit for at least six months if you are between 15 and 17 years of age.

teen_summary: A learner permit is available at 15. Applicants ages 15 to 17 hold it six months, complete driver education and 40 practice hours, and can be licensed at 16. Night and passenger limits apply to licensed drivers ages 16 and 17.

teen_points.text: Practice driving is 40 hours, with 10 of those hours after sunset.
teen_points.quote: Practice Driving Hours Required : 40 (10 after sunset)

teen_points.text: Ages 15 to 17 must hold the learner permit at least six months before applying for a license.
teen_points.quote: Have held your learner permit for at least six months if you are between 15 and 17 years of age.

teen_points.text: Licensed 16- and 17-year-olds may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. unless an exception applies.

teen_points.text: For six months or until age 18, non-immediate-family passengers are not allowed unless a licensed adult 21 or older is in the front seat.

name: Iowa
full_license_age_quote: How Do I Get a Full License? Available at age 17.
written_quote: Pass the knowledge and vision test.
written_detail: An instruction permit requires a knowledge test and a vision test. The knowledge test can be taken at a DMV, a county treasurer, at home with a parent proctor, or at some schools.
road_quote: Complete a drive test at the DMV if your driver’s education instructor requests it, or if you completed the Parent-Taught Driver’s Education Program.
road_detail: A drive test is required when the driver-education instructor requests it or when the applicant completed parent-taught driver education. It is not described as required for every intermediate applicant.
supervised_hours: 10 hours while holding the intermediate license, including 2 at night
supervised_quote: Complete 10 hours of supervised driving while holding your intermediate license.
holding_period: 12 months of instruction permit before an intermediate license
holding_quote: Have a valid instruction permit (or instruction permit and special minor’s restricted license ) for a total of 12 months.

fees.quote: Operator - Class C $4/year See expiration date chart

documents.summary: An instruction-permit applicant brings a primary identity document, proof of residency, and proof of Social Security number, plus parental consent if under 18.
documents.quote: Provide a primary form of identification, proof of residency, and proof of Social Security number.

documents.summary: REAL ID requires one document proving date of birth, identity, and lawful status, such as a passport or certified birth certificate.
documents.quote: Bring ONE document that provides proof of your date of birth, identity and lawful status like a valid passport or certified birth certificate.

real_id_summary: Iowa does not charge extra for a REAL ID gold star. Starting May 7, 2025, a REAL ID is required for domestic commercial flights and certain federal facilities.
real_id_quote: It does not cost more to get a card with a REAL ID star
transfer_summary: A person with a valid license from a U.S. state, territory, or Canada may not need Iowa’s knowledge test. A driving test may also be waived for those licenses. A minor’s out-of-state instruction permit alone still requires the Iowa knowledge test.
transfer_quote: or Canada, you may not need to take the knowledge test.
teen_summary: Iowa’s graduated system starts with an instruction permit at 14, an intermediate license at 16 after 12 months, and a full license at 17 after another 12 months. Unsupervised intermediate driving is limited to 5 a.m. to 12:30 a.m., and a parent may accept or waive a six-month passenger limit.

teen_points.text: The instruction permit is available at 14 after knowledge and vision tests and parental consent.
teen_points.quote: Be at least 14 years old.

teen_points.text: An intermediate license requires 12 months with a valid instruction permit, driver education, and a clean record for six months.
teen_points.quote: Have a valid instruction permit (or instruction permit and special minor’s restricted license ) for a total of 12 months.

teen_points.text: A full license is available at age 17.
teen_points.quote: How Do I Get a Full License? Available at age 17.

teen_points.text: Without a waiver, the first six months of an intermediate license allow no more than one unrelated minor passenger when driving unsupervised.
teen_points.quote: for the first six months you have your intermediate license, you cannot carry more than one minor passenger that is not a relative when driving without adult supervision.

teen_points.text: The intermediate license must be held at least 12 consecutive months immediately before a full license.
teen_points.quote: Keep your intermediate license for at least 12 consecutive months immediately before applying for a full license.

out_of_state_permit: A minor who brings only an out-of-state instruction permit must pass Iowa’s knowledge test. Time on that permit can count in some graduated-license paths.
out_of_state_permit_quote: If you have an out of state instruction permit only, you will need to pass the Iowa knowledge test.
curfew: Unsupervised intermediate driving only from 5 a.m. to 12:30 a.m.
curfew_quote: Drive without adult supervision between 5 a.m.
passengers: If accepted, no more than one unrelated minor passenger during the first six months of unsupervised intermediate driving
passengers_quote: for the first six months you have your intermediate license, you cannot carry more than one minor passenger that is not a relative when driving without adult supervision.
gaps: The under-18 instruction-permit page does not state a practice-hour total before the intermediate license. The 10-hour figure applies while the intermediate license is held, before a full license.
A drive test is conditional, so road_required is null rather than a yes-or-no for every teen.
The full-license page’s night-hour sentence is separate from the 10-hour sentence: “At least two of those hours must be between sunset and sunrise.”

name: Nevada
permit_age_quote: Nevada residents can apply for an instruction permit at age 15½.
written_quote: After passing the written test, you’ll get an instruction permit
written_detail: Teens pass a written test to receive the instruction permit. Under 18, they also submit school-attendance certification.
road_quote: Once you’ve completed driver education and practiced with your instruction permit, you’re ready for the road test.
road_detail: The road test comes after driver education, 50 supervised hours, and at least six months on the instruction permit, and the applicant must be 16.
supervised_quote: You must complete at least 50 hours of supervised driving, including 10 hours at night.
holding_quote: Hold a valid instruction permit for 6+ months

fees.quote: Return to the DMV to process your license Fee: $22.50

documents.summary: Unless the teen already has a Nevada ID, the application needs proof of identity, such as a certified U.S. birth certificate, plus attendance and residency documents.
documents.quote: Proof of Identity (e.g., Certified U.S. Birth Certificate)

documents.summary: A REAL ID needs identity, name-change proof if any, one Social Security document, and two Nevada residential-address documents.
documents.quote: Proof of identity (one document) And Proof of all name changes (if applicable) And Proof of Social Security Number (one document) And Two Proofs of Nevada Residential Address

real_id_summary: Nevada REAL ID is a version of the driver license or ID, marked with a gold star, that meets federal standards for domestic flights and secure federal facilities.
real_id_quote: A REAL ID is not a separate card; it is simply a version of your state-issued driver's license or ID that meets federal security standards.
transfer_summary: New residents must switch an out-of-state license to a Nevada license within 30 days and surrender the old license or ID.
transfer_quote: You must switch your out-of-state license to a Nevada one within 30 days of moving.
teen_summary: Nevada teens can get an instruction permit at 15½, complete driver education and 50 supervised hours, and test for a license at 16 after holding the permit six months. The license then has a six-month passenger limit and a 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. driving curfew.

teen_points.text: The instruction permit is available at age 15½ after the written and vision tests.
teen_points.quote: Nevada residents can apply for an instruction permit at age 15½.

teen_points.text: The road test requires age 16, six months on the permit, and 50 supervised hours.
teen_points.quote: Hold a valid instruction permit for 6+ months

teen_points.text: Supervised practice is 50 hours, including 10 at night, with a licensed driver who is 21 or older.
teen_points.quote: You must complete at least 50 hours of supervised driving, including 10 hours at night.

teen_points.text: For the first six months, the new license does not allow passengers under 18 except immediate family.
teen_points.quote: For the first 6 months: No passengers under 18 (except immediate family)

out_of_state_permit: Nevada honors valid instruction permits from other U.S. states and foreign countries. Drivers under 18 must follow Nevada teen restrictions while driving in the state.
out_of_state_permit_quote: Nevada honors valid licenses and instruction permits from other U.S. states and foreign countries.
curfew: No driving from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., except travel to or from school or work
curfew_quote: No driving between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m.
passengers: First 6 months: no passengers under 18 except immediate family
passengers_quote: For the first 6 months: No passengers under 18 (except immediate family)
gaps: The teen license page states the 10 p.m. curfew and the six-month passenger limit but does not state an age when every restriction ends, so full_license_age is null.

name: Arkansas
agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration, Office of Driver Services

teen_points.text: The learner’s license is for ages 14 and 15 and requires a licensed driver age 21 or older in the vehicle.
teen_points.quote: Learner’s license is for ages 14-15.

teen_points.text: The intermediate license is for ages 16 and 17.

teen_points.text: At 18, a teen may apply for a regular unrestricted license if the previous year of driving is clean.

name: Mississippi
agency: Mississippi Department of Public Safety, Driver Service Bureau
permit_age_quote: you must be at least 15 years old and be able to provide proof of being enrolled in school.
license_age_quote: the minimum age to receive a driver's license is 16 years old.
written_quote: All knowledge exams must be taken in person.
written_detail: Every applicant passes a knowledge exam in person, and an eye exam, before the learner’s permit is issued.
road_quote: A signed Waiver of Road Testing Affidavit

name: Kansas
agency: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles
permit_age_quote: Age: Minimum 14 years old Testing required: Vision.
license_age_quote: Age: Minimum 15 years old but less than 16
written_quote: Testing required: Vision. Written - or certificate of completion from driver education.
written_detail: An instruction permit requires a vision test and a written test, unless the applicant brings a driver-education completion certificate.

road_detail: The age-15 restricted license lists only a vision test. Less-restricted privileges at 16 require a written test and a drive test, or a driver-education completion certificate.
supervised_hours: 25 hours at age 15; 50 hours before age 16

fees.item: Photo fee when a new license is made
